source_generation.rationale: Standard present-perfect 'has' with the singular probe reads as a stable everyday complaint often continued with a mundane place; the nonstandard habitual 'be waking up' foregrounds an ongoing recurring problem, pushing the top next token toward a care-seeking destination. Term held constant, grammar shift alone reweights the continuation.

quadrants.B: She be waking up 'cause she got a urinary tract infection, so tonight she going to
quadrants.C: She keeps waking up because she has a bladder problem, so tonight she is going to
quadrants.D: She be waking up 'cause she got a bladder problem, so tonight she going to

top_prompt: Every morning before work he has severe anxiety, so today he finally called
bottom_prompt: Every morning before work he done had severe anxiety, so today he finally called

source_generation.rationale: Standard simple-present 'has' frames a routine feeling that could be continued with a casual recipient (a friend, work); the nonstandard completive 'done had' marks the state as fully realized and burdensome, steering the top next token toward a clinical recipient after 'called'. Only the aspect changes between frames.
